title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1,000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2,000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005. We report the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, present the bootstrap CI as a preregistered descriptive summary, explicitly label a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises reduced manual effort but raises safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that affect code and configuration generation, motivating architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our precise research question is: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The design intentionally isolates downstream interventions (validation and at‑most‑one repair) so that any paired difference is attributable to those downstream mechanisms rather than to first‑pass generation differences such as prompt engineering, constrained decoding, or sampling variance.

Contributions. (i) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus and archived validator traces. (ii) Full artifact‑grounded execution and analysis accounting that preserves shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one sampled initial generation reused by both arms) and documents the limited repair budget and model‑call accounting. (iii) Transparent preregistered confirmatory inference (exact two‑sided McNemar) with preregistered descriptive bootstrap summaries; we explicitly label any post‑hoc directional tests exploratory and discuss interpretive consequences of a high baseline success regime.
sections.related_work:
Existing surveys and controlled studies find that LLMs commonly exhibit hallucinations and prompt sensitivity that materially affect the correctness of generated artifacts, including code and configuration outputs [1],[2]. Work on constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning shows reductions in syntactic and executable errors for structured tasks, though much evidence originates outside NetOps and depends on the fidelity of the schema/tooling used to enforce constraints [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system papers emphasize verifier‑assisted repair, guarded architectures, and governance/proof‑carrying proposals; these works present prototypes and highlight that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and externally enforced protocols rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Our study complements that literature by preregistering a paired comparison whose estimand isolates the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation and a single limited repair call when the initial candidate is held constant across conditions. Importantly, the preregistered execution used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and did not execute any independent constrained‑prompt arm; therefore conclusions concern only the downstream validator/repair effect under identical initial candidates and do not generalize to interventions that change first‑pass generation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized and frozen before any hosted‑model invocation; its preregistration SHA‑256 is recorded in the execution manifest. Key preregistered elements: paired binary confirmatory design; task_count = 1000 deterministically drawn tasks from a synthetic stress corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries included a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) and preregistered sensitivity analyses for failure treatments.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. Under the archived generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled initial candidate (one shared generation). The guarded pipeline may deterministically reject that candidate via the validator and invoke at most one permitted repair call. Thus paired outcome differences can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and permitted repair(s). This design does not measure effects that would arise from independent first‑pass generations, alternative prompts, constrained decoding, or sampling‑variance interventions that were not executed.

Model/runtime configuration and temperature caveat. The declared provider/model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) as recorded in the archived model_configuration.json. That file records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was produced and deterministically shared across both conditions (shared_initial_provider stage). The validator was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (digital‑twin emulator style) and enforces workflow policies, required command presence/order, protected‑field noninterference, and returns a deterministic binary safe‑deploy verdict.

Task corpus and validator semantics. Tasks were selected deterministically from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile using the preregistered ordinal rule to produce 1000 unique task indices. Each task manifest contains initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). The deterministic validator parses the candidate command sequence, enforces manifest constraints, and emits structured validator traces archived per episode. Scoring used scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation yielding a binary validity outcome for paired analysis.

Execution, retries, missingness, and analysis fidelity. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and prespecified missingness treatments, and the registered analysis executor implemented the exact two‑sided McNemar test as the preregistered confirmatory analysis. Bootstrap resampling (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was preregistered as a descriptive secondary summary. Multiplicity adjustments for secondary hypothesis claims were preregistered but are not used to change the primary confirmatory claim here.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact‑grounded). Planned episodes = 2000; completed episodes = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000. Provider‑call accounting shows a shared_initial generation per task and a small number of repair invocations; total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). All deterministic reconciliation checks passed and no episode was excluded post‑hoc.

Paired outcomes and preregistered inference. The 2×2 paired contingency table is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold, so the preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered secondary descriptive summaries. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01]. This bootstrap interval was preregistered as descriptive only; with extremely sparse discordant counts the bootstrap percentile interval can exclude zero even when an exact two‑sided test is not < 0.05. A one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) yields p = 0.03125; because a directional one‑sided test was NOT prespecified in the frozen preregistration it is reported as exploratory/post‑hoc and does not change the preregistered confirmatory conclusion.

Repair diagnostics and representative traces. Five validator‑triggered repairs occurred; representative archived traces show repairs invoked for required_sequence violations or protected_interface touches where the repair call produced an accepted candidate upon revalidation. Raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces (where present), and validator traces are archived and referenced in the execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory vs descriptive hierarchy (explicit). The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar is the confirmatory analysis and did not reach two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap CI and any directional one‑sided tests are preregistered/descriptive or exploratory respectively; they do not overturn the preregistered confirmatory null. The bootstrap CI may exclude zero with very sparse discordant counts because percentile intervals can be sensitive to the discrete resampling distribution when n10 and n01 are small; the archived contingency table and bootstrap seed (1729) support this behavior.

Interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because both conditions reused the same initial sampled candidate, outcome differences arise only from deterministic validation and permitted repair(s). The observed five repairs demonstrate utile corrections in a small number of cases, but the overwhelmingly high baseline validity (0.995) implies very few discordant pairs and substantially reduced power to detect small absolute gains relative to the preregistered power assumptions (which assumed baseline ≈ 0.60). Thus the negative two‑sided confirmatory result primarily reflects low discordance under the studied corpus and model, not universal ineffectiveness of validator/repair architectures.

Threats to validity. Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on validator rule coverage; omitted semantic checks would inflate apparent success. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream effects but intentionally exclude independent generation interventions. External validity: a single model (gpt‑5‑mini) and a synthetic corpus limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments. Conclusion validity: near‑unity baseline yields sparse discordant counts and limits power for exact paired tests.

Operational implications and recommended preregistered follow‑ups. Artifact‑grounded evidence indicates deterministic validators plus bounded repair can avert some unsafe outcomes, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and repair budget. Preregistered follow‑ups that the archive supports: (i) run independent first‑pass generation arms (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding intervention effects; (ii) sweep repair budgets (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns per failure class; (iii) expand validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity; and (iv) include multiple model families. Each follow‑up should be preregistered with power calculations aligned to plausible baseline failure rates.
sections.conclusion:
In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The primary inferential outcome is the preregistered exact McNemar result; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration. These artifact‑grounded results indicate that downstream verifier/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Full preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run to support reproducibility and to guide preregistered follow‑ups that broaden model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

disclosure_statement: Declared model and provider: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). Orchestration and validator: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Preregistration identifier: cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any hosted‑model calls; preregistration SHA‑256 is recorded in the execution manifest). Immutable initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). After the autonomy lock, literature review, preregistration finalization, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revisions were performed by the autonomous research run; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
